studies.design: ONE registered two-part protocol, deliberately NOT split into two study records. Part 1 = open-label, single-arm Phase 2 (dose-finding/expansion); Part 2 = randomised 2:1, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicentre Phase 3. The registration also contains a vital-rate/QTc substudy and an extension phase. ClinicalTrials.gov design module for NCT02598661: allocation RANDOMIZED, intervention model PARALLEL, primary purpose TREATMENT, masking DOUBLE (participant, investigator); phases ['PHASE2','PHASE3']; arm groups are listed as 'Phase 2: Imetelstat Sodium', 'Phase 3: Imetelstat Sodium', 'Phase 3: Placebo', 'QTc Substudy: Imetelstat Sodium', 'QTc Substudy: Placebo', 'Extension Phase: Imetelstat Sodium', 'Extension Phase: Extended Follow-up'. The FDA review analyses the Phase 2 part, the Phase 3 part and a Phase 2+3 pool as three ANALYSIS GROUPINGS of this single trial; the Rytelo label reports only the Phase 3 part. All three groupings, plus the label statements derived from them, are deduplicated into this one trial record per hard rule 2.
studies.compound: imetelstat (GRN163L; drug substance imetelstat sodium; US trade name Rytelo)
studies.indication: transfusion-dependent IPSS low- or intermediate-1 risk (lower-risk) myelodysplastic syndrome, relapsed/refractory to or ineligible for erythropoiesis-stimulating agents; del(5q) and prior lenalidomide/HMA excluded
studies.population: Adults with LR-MDS requiring >=4 RBC units over 8 weeks in the 16 weeks before randomisation, with ANC >=1.5 x10^9/L and PLATELETS >=75 x10^9/L at entry. Label section 14.1: 'Patients were ineligible if they had del(5q) cytogenetic abnormality or had received prior treatment with lenalidomide or hypomethylating agents.' Phase 3 safety population median age 72 (range 44-87), 77% >=65 y, 30% >=75 y, 60% male, 81% White. ENTRY-CRITERION CAVEAT carried from the source (FDA review printed p218): because entry required platelets >=75 x10^9/L, none of the platelet results generalise to patients starting below 75 x10^9/L.
studies.n_enrolled: 289 (ClinicalTrials.gov actual enrolment for the whole registration, i.e. Phase 2 + Phase 3 + QTc substudy + extension). The regulatory analysis sets are smaller and must be used instead for any platelet denominator: Rytelo label section 14.1 'in 178 patients enrolled ... randomized in a 2:1 ratio to receive an intravenous infusion of RYTELO (n=118) 7.1 mg/kg or placebo (n=60)'; label section 6.1 safety population 'RYTELO (n=118) or placebo (n=59)' in 'a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial (IMerge) in 177 adult patients'. studies.n_analyzed_platelet: Phase 3: 118 imetelstat and 59 placebo (safety/laboratory analysis sets). Phase 2: 57 imetelstat. Phase 2 + Phase 3 pooled imetelstat: 175. These are the only platelet denominators used by the rows in this record; 175 = 118 + 57 and is a WITHIN-TRIAL pooling, not an extra population. Sub-denominators that appear inside individual rows: 77 (Phase 3 subjects who reached Grade 3/4 platelets, the denominator-at-risk for the bleeding-association analysis), 98 and 96 (Phase 3 subjects with evaluable aPTT and PT), 27 and 91 (Phase 3 imetelstat age subgroups <65 and >=65, which sum to 118), 51 (Phase 3 imetelstat subjects still contributing a platelet value at week 49-52), and ~17-19 (subjects with a value at cycle 13+). DISCREPANCY RESOLVED: review Table 97 prints the placebo denominator as N=60 while every other table uses N=59; the label shows why - 60 were randomised to placebo (section 14.1 efficacy population) but 59 received >=1 dose (section 6.1 safety population). studies.dose_regimen: 7.1 mg/kg every 4 weeks (28-day cycles) - this is the approved regimen and the dose expressed as imetelstat (free acid), as used throughout the FDA review, the Rytelo label and every curated row. UNIT-BASIS NOTE: the ClinicalTrials.gov record states a starting dose of 7.5 mg/kg because it expresses the dose as IMETELSTAT SODIUM ('Imetelstat sodium administered intravenously (IV), at a starting dose of 7.5 milligrams per kilogram (mg/kg), every 4 weeks'); 7.5 mg/kg imetelstat sodium and 7.1 mg/kg imetelstat are the registry and label renderings of the same administered amount, so the two numbers must not be treated as two dose levels. Label section 2.3 dose modifications: hold for platelets <50 x10^9/L, first reduction 5.6 mg/kg, second reduction 4.4 mg/kg q4w. The Phase 2 part permitted escalation (registry arm 'Phase 2: Imetelstat Sodium (Escalated to 9.4 mg/kg)', n=7 in the posted results).
studies.duration: Treat until progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal. Label section 6.1: 'The median time on treatment with RYTELO was 8 months (range, 0 to 38 months); 69% of patients were exposed to RYTELO for 24 weeks or longer and 45% were exposed for 48 weeks or longer.' FDA review gives median 7.8 months on treatment for the Phase 3 imetelstat arm and median 32.29 weeks for the Phase 2 cohort. Platelet observation window is defined by the protocol monitoring schedule (see platelet_endpoint_basis) and the by-cycle analysis runs to cycle 13+.

studies.notes:
MECHANISM FLAG (model eligibility): imetelstat is a 13-mer lipid(palmitoyl)-conjugated N3'->P5' THIO-PHOSPHORAMIDATE oligonucleotide that acts as a template antagonist of the RNA component of human telomerase (hTR), i.e. a competitive enzyme inhibitor, NOT a hybridisation-driven gene-silencing PS/2'-MOE antisense drug. Its thrombocytopenia is ON-TARGET MYELOSUPPRESSION: telomerase inhibition in haematopoietic (including megakaryocytic) progenitors of a diseased marrow, which is mechanistically distinct from the PS-backbone platelet effects (PF4-dependent / immune-mediated and acute non-immune platelet-binding mechanisms) that the PS-ASO rows in this dataset measure. Three internal lines of evidence support the on-target reading rather than a backbone/platelet-binding reading: (i) the cytopenia is pan-myeloid, not platelet-selective - at the recommended dose neutrophils 89%, leukocytes 92%, platelets 94% (FDA review Table 78); (ii) the dose-response is population-confounded by underlying marrow disease, the reviewer stating 'patients with MDS are more vulnerable to cytopenias compared to patients with solid tumors' (printed p284), which is a progenitor-reserve argument, not a chemistry argument; (iii) events are rapidly and repeatedly reversible on dose hold (median recovery 1.3 weeks) and recur on redosing (212 events in 77 patients), the kinetics of cyclical progenitor suppression. CONSEQUENCE: these rows must NOT be pooled with PS-ASO platelet rows for any sequence- or backbone-attribution model, and must not be used as a positive class member in a 'PS-backbone causes thrombocytopenia' classifier. They are legitimate for modality-breadth description and for dose/exposure-response methodology only.

MDS3001 Phase 3 imetelstat (118) + MDS3001 Phase 2 imetelstat (57) = the 175 'Pooled' column; that 175 sits INSIDE the integrated-summary recommended-dose band of 190; the 190/54/296 bands sit inside the overall development programme; and the placebo comparator column printed against the pooled dose-band tables (6/59, 1/59, 7/59, 0/59) IS the MDS3001 Phase 3 placebo arm, not an additional control group. SCOPE OF THIS RECORD: all 62 curated measurement rows that describe the MDS3001 Phase 2 cohort, the MDS3001 Phase 3 randomised comparison, the MDS3001 Phase 2+3 pool, the MDS3001-only exposure-response analyses, and the two Rytelo-label rows. They are one trial under hard rule 2. This is the ONLY unit in the imetelstat cluster for which patient-level platelet outcomes are reported at the study level.

WHY THE PHASE 2 AND PHASE 3 PARTS ARE NOT COUNTED AS TWO TRIALS: both are arms of registration NCT02598661 and appear as arm groups of one record ('Phase 2: Imetelstat Sodium', 'Phase 3: Imetelstat Sodium', 'Phase 3: Placebo'), with one EudraCT number and one sponsor protocol id. Counting them separately would double-count the registration. The cost of that choice is recorded here so a consumer can re-split if it needs cohort grain: the Phase 2 part is open-label and uncontrolled, the Phase 3 part is placebo-controlled, and the two have different platelet denominators (57 vs 118/59) and different results (e.g. Grade 3/4 thrombocytopenia 54.4% Phase 2 vs 61.9% Phase 3; serious thrombocytopenia 3.5% Phase 2 vs 0% Phase 3; discontinuation for thrombocytopenia 12.3% Phase 2 vs 3.4% Phase 3). Treating a Phase 2 row and a Phase 3 row as independent replications is defensible as internal replication but they are NOT independent trials.

LABEL ROWS DEDUPLICATED, NOT TYPED AS label_summary: TMSR690 and TMSR691 (source SRC-82B0FA, the Rytelo SPL) and TMSR648 (the FDA review's reproduction of the agreed section 5.1 text) are statements ABOUT this trial, not a separate unspecified label summary. The label itself says 'In the clinical trial' (singular) and section 6.1 names it: 'a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial (IMerge) in 177 adult patients'. The cell-for-cell match of the label's 48/31/33/24 by-cycle percentages to review Table 85 removes any doubt. Under hard rule 4 a label summary is typed separately only when the underlying population is unspecified; here it is specified, so hard rule 2 (deduplicate) governs.

UNRESOLVED NUMERIC DISCREPANCY, FLAGGED NOT FIXED (defect found in the underlying rows' source, not in the rows): TMSR648 carries 65.2% from the FDA review's Section 20 Labeling Recommendations table (printed p345, the text proposed/agreed at review time), whereas the APPROVED label as published states 65% (verified by fetching the SPL). 65.2% does not reconcile by ordinary rounding with any numerator/denominator pair printed elsewhere in the review - 77/118 is 65.25% which rounds to 65.3, and 65/8 percent figures in Tables 77 and 85 are printed to zero decimals. The exact numerator behind the 65.2% rendering is NOT printed anywhere in the sources held, so it is left as the source states it and NO arithmetic reconstruction is asserted. Both values are recorded_as_printed at their own loci and neither row was altered.

PART OF THE REGISTRATION NOT REPRESENTED BY ANY CURATED ROW: the vital-rate/QTc substudy. Its posted results carry their own thrombocytopenia counts (otherEvents 'Thrombocytopenia': QTc substudy imetelstat 25 of 35, QTc crossover imetelstat 9 of 14, QTc placebo 3 of 18) which appear in NO curated row and in no FDA review table used here. This is a known, bounded coverage gap in the cluster, recorded rather than silently filled. It also means the registration contains more imetelstat-exposed, platelet-monitored subjects than the 175 the dataset describes.

ROWS KEPT HERE THAT ARE NOT PLATELET-SPECIFIC: TMSR671 (aPTT prolonged 26% vs 17%) and TMSR672 (PT prolonged 34% vs 30%) are coagulation-time readouts the curator already flagged is_platelet_specific FALSE. They belong to this trial and are kept in its measurement_ids so the row inventory balances, but they must not be read as platelet endpoints. They are the one place where a classical sulfurised-oligonucleotide class effect could have shown itself, and the excess over placebo is small (+9 aPTT, +4 PT, one Grade 3-4 event per arm).

TWO ROWS CARRY readout_value 'TBD' BY DESIGN AND ARE STILL ASSIGNED HERE: TMSR641 (Figure 36 mean platelet trajectory) and TMSR642 (Figure 4 Grade 3/4 incidence by Cmax quartile). Both are plotted figures with no printed data table; the curator correctly refused to digitise them. They are assignable to this trial even though they carry no value, so they are NOT unassignable.

DOSE/EXPOSURE-RESPONSE EVIDENCE INSIDE THIS TRIAL (the scientifically load-bearing content): review Table 123 gives a significant positive exposure-response between Cycle 1 Cmax and Grade 3/4 thrombocytopenia in MDS3001 (pLRT 0.0192 univariate, 0.0195 multivariate) with AUC only a trend (0.0894/0.0594) and Cavg null (0.998); Table 124's final multiple logistic model retains Cmax (slope 0.0166 logit per ug/mL, 95% CI 0.00259-0.0317, p=0.0252) and BASELINE PLATELET COUNT (slope -0.00632, 95% CI -0.00952 to -0.00353, p=0.0000327), i.e. a low starting platelet count predicts severe thrombocytopenia MORE strongly than exposure does. The contrast the reviewer draws is important for mechanism: in the same trial no exposure metric predicted Grade 3/4 NEUTROPENIA (Cmax 0.145, AUC 0.827, Cavg 0.749), so within MDS3001 the exposure-driven cytopenia is specifically the platelet one even though the overall cytopenia pattern is pan-myeloid. FDA added the exposure statement to label section 12.2 and issued PMR #5 requiring a randomised trial of at least two dosages.

Three internal lines of evidence support the on-target reading rather than a backbone/platelet-binding reading: (i) the cytopenia is pan-myeloid, not platelet-selective - at the recommended dose neutrophils 89%, leukocytes 92%, platelets 94% (FDA review Table 78); (ii) the dose-response is population-confounded by underlying marrow disease, the reviewer stating 'patients with MDS are more vulnerable to cytopenias compared to patients with solid tumors' (printed p284), which is a progenitor-reserve argument, not a chemistry argument; (iii) events are rapidly and repeatedly reversible on dose hold (median recovery 1.3 weeks) and recur on redosing (212 events in 77 patients), the kinetics of cyclical progenitor suppression. CONSEQUENCE: these rows must NOT be pooled with PS-ASO platelet rows for any sequence- or backbone-attribution model, and must not be used as a positive class member in a 'PS-backbone causes thrombocytopenia' classifier. They are legitimate for modality-breadth description and for dose/exposure-response methodology only.

notes:
SCOPE AND HEADLINE. 79 curated measurement rows for imetelstat (oligo_id TOLG070) resolve to ONE human clinical trial that actually reports patient-level platelet outcomes - MDS3001 / IMerge, NCT02598661 - plus THREE pooled analyses that are not trials, plus FOUR further registered trials that exist in this registry only because one pooled analysis enumerates them by protocol id. Totals: 8 study records; 5 registered_trial records, every one carrying a registry id verified by fetching the ClinicalTrials.gov API on 2026-10-01; 3 pooled_analysis records; 0 case reports, cohorts, spontaneous-report series, expanded-access or label-summary units; 0 unassignable rows. 62 of the 79 rows belong to MDS3001, 15 to the integrated dose-band pooling, 1 to the 391-patient monotherapy pool and 1 to the pooled exposure-response analysis. FOUR of the five trials carry no measurement rows at all, so the row count tells you almost nothing about how many trials underlie this cluster - which is the point of the exercise.

THE TWO TRIALS THE LEAD CURATOR ASKED FOR, VERIFIED. IMerge = MDS3001 = NCT02598661 (Phase 2/3, lower-risk MDS, Geron; actual enrolment 289). IMbark = MYF2001 = NCT02426086 (Phase 2, myelofibrosis relapsed/refractory to JAK inhibitor, Geron; actual enrolment 107). Neither alias appears in the registry's own acronym field, so both name-to-id links were established from primary or peer-reviewed text rather than assumed: IMerge from the Rytelo USPI section 14.1 ('a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial (IMerge; NCT02598661)') and IMbark from Blood Advances 2023 (PMID 37216228 / PMC10424149, full text via Europe PMC: 'A phase 2 study entitled IMbark (NCT02426086)'), with the primary IMbark publication PMID 34138638 independently citing NCT02426086. The protocol aliases MDS3001 and MYF2001 did not need inference at all - they are the registrations' own secondary ids (63935937MDS3001 and 63935937MYF2001).

THE CENTRAL JUDGEMENT: PHASE 2 AND PHASE 3 ARE ONE TRIAL, NOT TWO. The FDA review presents MDS3001 Phase 2 (57 imetelstat, open-label), MDS3001 Phase 3 (118 imetelstat vs 59 placebo, randomised double-blind) and a Phase 2+3 pool (175) as three analysis groupings, and most of the 62 rows are tagged to one of the three. It is tempting to count two or three trials. They are ONE: one registration, one sponsor protocol id, one EudraCT number, and the registry lists 'Phase 2: Imetelstat Sodium', 'Phase 3: Imetelstat Sodium' and 'Phase 3: Placebo' as arm groups of the single record NCT02598661. Counting them separately would double-count the registration. The cost of the choice is written into the MDS3001 record so a consumer can re-split to cohort grain if it needs to, together with the warning that a Phase 2 row and a Phase 3 row are internal replication, not independent trials.

SECOND JUDGEMENT: THE LABEL ROWS ARE THE SAME TRIAL. Rows TMSR690 and TMSR691 come from the Rytelo SPL and TMSR648 from the FDA review's reproduction of the agreed section 5.1 text. Under hard rule 2 they are deduplicated into MDS3001 rather than typed label_summary, because the label specifies its population ('a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial (IMerge) in 177 adult patients', section 6.1) and because the label's by-cycle percentages 48 / 31 / 33 / 24 are cell-for-cell the review's Table 85 rows Cycles 1-3, 4-6, 7-12, 13+. That match is the hard link, and it was verified by fetching the live SPL, not recalled. Hard rule 4's label_summary type is for UNSPECIFIED label summaries; this is not one. Consequence for the dataset: the Rytelo label contributes no additional trial and no additional patient.

MECHANISM - THE FINDING THAT MOST AFFECTS MODEL ELIGIBILITY. Imetelstat is a 13-mer lipid-conjugated N3'->P5' thio-phosphoramidate oligonucleotide that competitively inhibits telomerase by binding the template region of hTR. Its thrombocytopenia is ON-TARGET MYELOSUPPRESSION of haematopoietic progenitors, NOT the PS-backbone platelet effect the rest of this dataset measures. Three internal lines of evidence support that reading and are recorded in each study record: (i) the cytopenia is pan-myeloid rather than platelet-selective - at the recommended dose neutrophils 89%, leukocytes 92%, platelets 94% (review Table 78); (ii) incidence tracks the patient's marrow reserve, the reviewer stating 'patients with MDS are more vulnerable to cytopenias compared to patients with solid tumors' (printed p284), which is a progenitor-reserve argument, not a chemistry argument; (iii) the kinetics are those of cyclical progenitor suppression - median onset 6 weeks, median recovery 1.3 weeks, and recurrence on redosing (212 Grade 3/4 events in 77 patients). ONE COUNTERVAILING OBSERVATION IS RECORDED HONESTLY RATHER THAN SUPPRESSED: within MDS3001 the exposure-response is specific to platelets - Cycle 1 Cmax predicts Grade 3/4 thrombocytopenia (pLRT 0.0192 univariate, 0.0195 multivariate) while NO exposure metric predicts Grade 3/4 neutropenia (Cmax 0.145, AUC 0.827, Cavg 0.749). That platelet specificity of the exposure effect sits awkwardly with a purely pan-myeloid account and is flagged rather than explained away. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE: these rows must not be pooled with PS-ASO platelet rows for sequence- or backbone-attribution modelling, and must not serve as positive-class members in a 'PS backbone causes thrombocytopenia' classifier. They are legitimate for modality-breadth description and for dose/exposure-response methodology.

NON-ADDITIVITY (hard rule 7) - THE EASIEST WAY TO CORRUPT THIS CLUSTER. The denominators are nested. 118 + 57 = the 175 'Pooled' column; 175 sits inside the 190-patient recommended-dose band; 54 / 190 / 296 sit inside the overall programme; MDS3001 sits inside the 391-patient monotherapy pool and inside the pooled exposure-response dataset; and the placebo column printed beside the pooled dose-band tables (6/59, 1/59, 7/59, 0/59) IS the MDS3001 Phase 3 placebo arm, not an extra control group. Never sum any two of 118, 57, 175, 190, 54, 296, 391, 540. One further trap inside IMbark: its posted-results groups are 48, 59 and 12, but the 12 dose-escalated patients are a SUBSET of the 48, so 48+59+12 = 119 is not its enrolment (107 is).

POOLED ANALYSES AND CONSTITUENT DISCIPLINE (hard rule 3). Three pooled_analysis records, each with its constituents_identifiable set from what its own locus actually prints, never from what seemed likely. (a) The 391-patient monotherapy haematologic-malignancy pool is the ONLY locus that enumerates its members - MDS3001, CP14B013, CP14B015, CP14B019, MYF2001 - so it is the only one with constituents_identifiable 'yes', and it is the sole reason the four extra trial records exist. All five protocol ids were resolved to verified registrations by API fetch, and all five turned out to be Geron imetelstat studies in haematologic malignancies, which is a consistency check on the stated membership. Sanity check only, not asserted: 175+107+80+20+13 = 395 against the printed 391. (b) The ISS dose-band pooling and (c) the pooled exposure-response dataset get 'partial': MDS3001 is positively identifiable in each (the standard dose band is its regimen and contains its 175 patients, and its own row sits directly above the pooled exposure-response row in the same table), but neither locus lists its studies, and the imetelstat programme contains many solid-tumour protocols that were NOT enumerated and were therefore NOT created. No constituent record was invented and no study was placed in a pool by inference.

ONE POOLING DECISION WORTH STATING: the 15 dose-band rows could have been split into three records by dose band or two by table. They are one record. The three bands are strata of a single pooling and the two tables (Table 78, laboratory; Table 99, adverse events) report two ascertainment datasets on the SAME patients - evidenced by their identical denominators 54 / 190 / 296. Splitting by band would invent three study units; splitting by table would double-count 540 patients.

METHODOLOGICAL WARNING ABOUT THE DOSE-RESPONSE, FOR ANY CONSUMER FITTING A CURVE. Thrombocytopenia by dose band is NON-MONOTONIC in both ascertainment routes: 21% -> 73% -> 62% for adverse-event terms, 48% -> 94% -> 74% for laboratory values. Both fall at the highest dose. This is confounding by indication, stated by the reviewer: the high-dose band is enriched for solid-tumour and non-MDS patients with better marrow reserve ('the relationship is confounded by the wide variety of underlying conditions being treated', printed p309). A model fitting dose to these three bands without conditioning on indication will recover a spurious inverted-U. The supporting contrast: the HAEMORRHAGE endpoints in the same table ARE monotonic (any-grade 22 -> 26 -> 52%; Grade 3-4 1.9 -> 6 -> 21%; fatal 0 -> 0 -> 1.7%), because bleeding depends on achieved platelet depth rather than on starting marrow reserve. The clean dose comparison in this cluster is IMbark, where dose WAS randomised: thrombocytopenia 11/48 (23%) at 4.7 mg/kg versus 29/59 (49%) at 9.4 mg/kg.

NO FABRICATED NEGATIVES (hard rule 5). Every zero retained here is a zero at a printed denominator in a table whose same endpoint is non-zero elsewhere: fatal haemorrhage 0/54 and 0/190 against 5/296; Grade 3/4 and serious bleeding 0/118 in MDS3001 Phase 3 against 2/57 in the Phase 2 cohort; Grade 5 fatal thrombocytopenia 0/118, 0/59, 0/57. These are measured negatives for those endpoints at those exposures, not reporting silence, and the curated rows already quote the confirming text ('There were no Grade 5 events of thrombocytopenia'; 'None of the subjects in the MDS3001 Phase 3 imetelstat group had Grade 3 or Grade 4 or serious bleeding events associated with Grade 3/4 decreased platelets'). No row was converted into a negative anywhere in this file. Two trials, CP14B013 and CP14B015, have platelet_endpoint_evaluable 'partial' precisely because their platelet endpoints cannot be shown to have been assessed study-specifically - that is recorded as a limit, not filled in.

DEFECTS AND DISCREPANCIES FOUND IN THE UNDERLYING ROWS AND THEIR SOURCES - FLAGGED, NOT SILENTLY FIXED. (1) RESOLVED: TMSR674 notes that review Table 97 prints the placebo denominator as N=60 while every other table uses N=59. The label explains it - 60 were randomised to placebo (section 14.1, efficacy population) but 59 received at least one dose (section 6.1, safety population). Table 97 uses the randomised set. Neither figure is an error and the rows should not be 'corrected'. (2) UNRESOLVED AND LEFT AS PRINTED: TMSR648 carries 65.2% from the review's Section 20 Labeling Recommendations table, but the APPROVED label states 65% (verified by fetching the SPL), and 65.2% does not reconcile by ordinary rounding with any numerator/denominator pair printed in the review - 77/118 is 65.25%, which rounds to 65.3. The numerator behind 65.2% is not printed anywhere in the sources held, so no arithmetic reconstruction is asserted and the row is untouched. (3) COVERAGE GAP, now bounded: registration NCT02598661 contains a vital-rate/QTc substudy whose posted results carry their own thrombocytopenia counts (imetelstat 25/35, crossover imetelstat 9/14, placebo 3/18). No curated row and no review table used here covers it, so the registration holds more imetelstat-exposed, platelet-monitored subjects than the 175 the dataset describes. (4) COVERAGE GAP: CP14B019 (NCT01731951) has posted results showing 'Platelet count decreased' in 80 of 80 patients across all six arms, serious in 32 of 80 - the highest platelet-event incidence in the entire imetelstat programme - and the curated dataset holds no row from it. (5) LABEL CONSISTENCY, NOT A DEFECT: the 'monotherapy' pool includes CP14B013, whose registered arms are imetelstat 'with or without lenalidomide standard of care'; whether those subjects were excluded from the monotherapy grouping is not stated in any source held. (6) INTERPRETATION TRAP: the same pool includes CP14B015 in essential thrombocythemia / polycythemia vera, where baseline platelets are pathologically high and platelet lowering is the INTENDED effect - an efficacy endpoint pooled into a toxicity incidence. 20 of 391 patients, so small quantitatively, but it inverts the sign of interpretation and must travel with the 46.8% figure.

UNIT-BASIS NOTE THAT WILL OTHERWISE BE READ AS A SECOND DOSE LEVEL. ClinicalTrials.gov records imetelstat doses as imetelstat SODIUM (7.5 / 4.7 / 9.4 mg/kg) while the FDA review, the Rytelo label and every curated row use imetelstat free acid (7.1 / 4.4 / 8.9 mg/kg). 7.5 mg/kg sodium and 7.1 mg/kg free acid are two renderings of the same administered amount, not two dose levels, and the curated rows' 4.4 / 7.1 / 8.9 triple maps onto the registry's 4.7 / 7.5 / 9.4 triple. The ISS dose bands '<7.1', '7.1' and '>7.1 mg/kg per 4 weeks' are recorded verbatim as strings; NO midpoint was invented for the open-ended bands.

EXTERNAL CONFIRMATION OF THE CURATION ITSELF. The ClinicalTrials.gov posted results for NCT02598661 reproduce the curated rows independently of the FDA document: adverse-event term 'Thrombocytopenia', Phase 3 imetelstat 89 of 118 and Phase 3 placebo 6 of 59 (= TMSR625's 75.4% vs 10.2%); serious thrombocytopenia 0 of 118 and 0 of 59 (= TMSR621); and 2 of 50 serious in the Phase 2 no-escalation group plus 0 of 7 in the escalated group, i.e. 2 of 57 (= TMSR620). The Phase 2 any-grade counts 33 of 50 plus 2 of 7 give 35 of 57 (61.4%), exactly the figure TMSR623's note records. The curated rows survive an independent check against a source the curator did not use.

CONVENTIONS. n_enrolled and n_analyzed_platelet are strings throughout, matching the convention already set by registry_volanesorsen.json in this directory, because most of these denominators are structured (per part, per arm, per dose band, with overlap warnings) and collapsing them to one integer would destroy exactly the information hard rule 7 exists to protect. registry_id is '' for pooled analyses, which cannot have one. Where a value is genuinely unknown it is the string 'TBD'; 'NOT_REGISTERED' is used NOWHERE in this file, because every trial unit here is in fact registered and verified, and no claim about pre-registration-era status was needed.

LIMITATIONS. (a) Neither source document (SRC-EAC193, the FDA NDA 217779 multi-discipline review; SRC-82B0FA, the Rytelo SPL) was re-fetched as a PDF; the review's content is taken from the curated rows' verbatim transcriptions and printed-page loci, which are detailed enough to quote but were not re-read against the original. The label WAS re-fetched and re-read directly (DailyMed SPL setid b0fab7ca-e578-43c5-9df6-bdaff4182257, version 4, published 2026-04-27), and sections 2.3, 5.1, 6.1 and 14.1 are quoted from that fetch. (b) No EMA assessment report was consulted; imetelstat's EU status and any EPAR platelet data are outside what was verified here, so no EU locus is asserted. (c) The pooled exposure-response dataset's N and study list are not printed in the material held and were not estimated. (d) CP14B013 and CP14B015 have no posted results and no per-study platelet data anywhere in the sources held; their platelet status is 'partial' and stays there. (e) Per-study platelet contributions to the 391-patient and 540-patient poolings are not printed and were not reconstructed. (f) Registry-posted adverse-event results were used to VERIFY that platelet endpoints were assessed and to cross-check curated numbers; they were NOT imported as new measurement rows, which is outside this task's remit. Where that leaves real evidence unharvested (the QTc substudy, and all of CP14B019) it is recorded above as a bounded, actionable gap.
